sc: Membranes ruptured > 18 h, maternal fever, day-1 poor feeding and distress → Early-onset sepsis (GBS)
Day-10 vesicles and seizures, mother had genital sores → Neonatal herpes: IV aciclovir
Home delivery, stops sucking on day 6, spasms, opisthotonus, alert → Neonatal tetanus
f: Poor feeding, lethargy, temperature instability (often hypothermia), apnoea, RD, jaundice, bulging fontanelle
< 72 h: GBS, E. coli, Listeria (from mother) · > 72 h: staph (lines), gram-negatives, hospital
Blood culture (best) · CBC, CRP · LP · urine (late onset) · chest X-ray
Ampicillin + gentamicin ≥ 10 days · meningitis: cefotaxime ≥ 3 weeks · avoid ceftriaxone in jaundice
CMV (commonest, periventricular calcification, deafness) · toxoplasma (hydrocephalus, diffuse calcification) · rubella (cataract, deafness, PDA) · syphilis (snuffles, rash on palms)
Gonococcal eye day 2–5: ceftriaxone · chlamydia day 5–14: erythromycin · omphalitis: IV cloxacillin + gentamicin
trap: Septic newborns are often hypothermic, not febrile · calcification around the ventricles = CMV, scattered = toxoplasma · neonatal tetanus: baby stays alert between spasms
